subject: Pilot success metrics & gating — operational runbook
messages:
From: Jamal Reed <jamal.reed@pioneerhealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Tan <emily.tan@pioneerhealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-25 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot kickoff — need explicit success metrics

Sergio,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We had a short internal sync and the execs want a tight operational runbook that ties deliverables to clear pass/fail signals for a 6-week pilot.

Specifically they asked: 1) what exact metrics will prove this reduces triage time by >=25% (we need numeric thresholds), 2) what are the stoplight gates where we would pause/terminate the pilot, and 3) what test cases will you run against our representative data to demonstrate behavior coverage.

Can you propose a one-page stoplight-style template and a short list of acceptance checks we can review with compliance? We need something we can show on Friday.

— Jamal
Sr. Director, Automation & AI
Pioneer Health

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: Jamal Reed <jamal.reed@pioneerhealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-25 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot kickoff — need explicit success metrics

Thanks Jamal — great prompt. Draft attached: "MAP-stoplight-template.xlsx" and a compact test-case doc "pilot-test-cases.md" (see attachments). High level summary below so the execs have something to scan quickly.

TL;DR (one-line): Target 25–30% reduction in triage latency on end-to-end tickets; stop if false-positive rate > 12% or if PII leakage tests fail any critical case.

Proposed success metrics (measurable):
- Mean triage latency (baseline vs pilot): target >= 25% reduction in median time-to-first-action on flagged records (baseline measured over 30 days).
- Accuracy by class: precision on automation recommendations >= 78% across top 5 categories (billing, pre-auth, intake, scheduling, clinical-coding).
- Regression guardrails: no more than 2% increase in escalation rate to human agents vs baseline.

Stoplight gating (green/amber/red):
- Green: all metric thresholds met or exceeded AND no PII incidents in synthetic+sampled data runs.
- Amber: one metric misses target by up to 10% or non-critical PII flags (requires remediation plan + 1-week extension).
- Red: precision drop > 12% OR PII leakage on critical cases OR sustained latency regression > 5% — immediate pause and exec review.

Acceptance test set (examples):
1) Representative throughput run: 2,000 anonymized tickets/day for 72 hours — measure latency and caching behavior.
2) Edge-case prompt battery: 40 curated prompts that historically cause hallucination/PII leak.
3) Class-specific precision tests: 200 labeled items per top category to compute precision/recall.
4) Failover & fallback: inject model/region failover to verify automatic routing and SLA behavior.

Attachments contain the stoplight spreadsheet with thresholds, owner fields, and the detailed test-case list with expected pass/fail criteria and sample inputs.

Next steps: if this looks good we propose a Monday 9am sync to finalize owners and sign the MAP. If Pioneer wants, Marissa will run a pre-flight on a small sample (2-3 days) ahead of full pilot.

--
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.ai
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
To: Jamal Reed <jamal.reed@pioneerhealth.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-26 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot kickoff — need explicit success metrics

Jamal / team — small additions from a product/ops perspective:
- Add a gating criterion for cache warmup: if median token latency doesn't improve after first 24 hours of steady traffic, we classify that as Amber (likely config/tuning).
- Add an audit log completeness check: every inference must map to a request id and contain model version metadata; failure rate > 1% is Red.

I've annotated the spreadsheet (column H) with owners: Product Ops (Lauren) will own cache checks; Marissa will run the synthetic PII battery.

Happy to walk through on Friday.

— Lauren
Director, Product Operations
From: Jamal Reed <jamal.reed@pioneerhealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Tan <emily.tan@pioneerhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-27 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot kickoff — need explicit success metrics

Appreciate the concrete template — that helps. A couple of quick clarifications from compliance:
1) For PII battery: can you confirm redaction vs blocking behavior? We require proof that the system never returns raw SSNs or full MRNs in responses (even in edge cases).
2) For the throughput run: do you have a plan to simulate our traffic distribution (we have a bimodal arrival pattern with spikes at 8am and 3pm PST)?

Also — can Marissa run the edge-case prompt battery on a small sanitized sample we can provide? We'll share a secure SFTP location for the items. Friday still works for an executive readout if the doc is final.

— Jamal

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Jamal Reed <jamal.reed@pioneerhealth.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-29 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot kickoff — need explicit success metrics

Hi Jamal — quick operational notes and confirmation:
- PII handling: Redwood will run the battery in two modes: (A) redaction-first (we redact tokens matching PII regex before sending), and (B) blocking-with-explain (reject and return a safe error message). Results will include logs showing detected tokens (masked) and the chosen behavior. We will never include raw SSNs/MRNs in outputs during any test run.
- Traffic simulation: we will run a distributed load test that follows the hourly distribution you shared. We'll seed the pilot with a 48-hour warmup that includes synthetic spikes at 8am and 3pm PST to validate autoscaling and cache warmup.
- Logistics: please drop the sanitized sample to the SFTP by EOD Thursday. I'll run the edge-case battery on Friday morning and share a short report by 2pm so you have something for the exec readout.

Attached: final MAP spreadsheet (MAP-stoplight-template.xlsx) and the detailed test cases (pilot-test-cases.md).

Next steps (owners / dates):
- Jamal: confirm SFTP + share sample (due 2027-04-30)
- Marissa: run PII battery & throughput pre-flight (2027-04-30 to 2027-05-01)
- Lauren: confirm Product Ops checklists and alert thresholds (2027-05-03)
- Sergio: coordinate exec readout slide (2027-04-30)

Thanks — looking forward.

— Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference
